images.caption: Figure 2:Xp-Data curation pipeline.Heterogeneous human and robot recordings pass through five stages. (1)Data sources: 14 public human egocentric datasets, 6,000 h of in-house four-camera recordings, and 13 public robot datasets. (2)Video filteringremoves low-quality or task-irrelevant clips with a vision-language model. (3)Multimodal annotationproduces geometry (metric camera poses via SLAM and DA3[69]), kinematics (human hands via WiLoR[91]and MANO[96], robot keypoints via URDF forward kinematics, manual annotation, and correction), and semantics (hierarchical task, subtask, and atomic-action captions). (4)Quality checkverifies completeness, correctness, and cross-modal consistency, pairing automated checks with a caption cascade (Gemini[25]annotation, Qwen[6]verification, and human review). (5)Training-clip constructioncuts quality-verified subtasks into standardized 81-frame,640×480640\times 480, 16 fps multimodal clips, yielding the unified cross-embodiment corpus.

Figure 3:Overview of Xp-Data.Top: caption terms. Middle: environment and task distributions for robot (inner ring) and human (outer ring) data. Bottom: unified skeleton annotations across human hands, dexterous robot hands, and parallel grippers.

Figure 4:Overview of Ropedia W0.Left:Human pose annotations and robot forward kinematics provide kinematic structure and wrist poses; manual robot-keypoint annotation and correction align robot skeletons with the observed images.Middle:Camera trajectories are encoded as Plücker-ray maps, while manipulation is represented by skeleton maps, optionally augmented with wrist-pose and wide-FOV renderings.Right:A video diffusion transformer predicts future frames from an initial image, a text prompt, and these control signals. Pixel-aligned conditions are fused through additive projections, while wide-FOV features are injected via cross-attention.

Figure 5:Overview of Xp-Teleop.About one hour of dexterous-humanoid teleoperation spanning six everyday household activity groups, from tidying and food preparation to laundry and cleaning (a). Each take is a long-horizon episode that chains locomotion with manipulation, such as putting objects into a box or folding a jacket on the bed (b). Takes are recorded as a single synchronized multimodal stream (egocentric RGB-D, 6-DoF camera pose, projected hand/robot skeletons and masks, 29-joint robot state, time-aligned language segments, per-hand tactile, and head IMU; c), and their 543 annotated segments are dominated by loco-manipulation verbs such asreach,walk, andgrasp(d).

Figure 10:World–action modeling.(a) Real-robot executions of the policy initialized from Ropedia W0, shown as four chronological pairs of recorded keyframes with different objects, containers, and placements.
(b) Aggregate real-robot task progress for Ropedia W0 initialization, FastWAM[131], and theΨ0\Psi_{0}[117]policy.

Figure 11:Live teleoperation with Ropedia W0.On-site recordings show the headset user and the monitor displaying model-generated feedback.
Five chronological keyframes show interactions with human (top) and robot (bottom) embodiments.

Figure S2:Motion annotations on the egocentric human data.Projected 21-point hand skeletons are overlaid on each frame, with the two hands drawn in different colors; the inset shows the camera trajectory of the surrounding window.

Figure S3:Example frames from the robot data in Xp-Data.The grid spans dexterous five-finger hands, three-finger hands, and parallel grippers on single-arm, dual-arm, and humanoid platforms, across household, retail, industrial, and tabletop scenes.

Figure S4:Motion annotations on the robot data.Image-aligned skeletons combine embodiment-native FK projections with manual keypoint annotation and correction (Sec.3), covering dexterous hands and grippers; the inset shows the camera trajectory of the surrounding window.

Figure S5:Distillation of Ropedia W0 into a few-step causal student.Top: causal distillation initializes the few-step autoregressive generator.
Bottom: asymmetric DMD updates the causal generatorGθG_{\theta}using a frozen bidirectional real-score teacher and an online-trained bidirectional fake-score model. The diagram illustrates the A14B MoE backbone; the 5B model follows an analogous procedure with a dense backbone. LongLive subsequently extends the few-step model for long-video streaming (Fig.S6).

Figure S6:LongLive-based streaming with the distilled student.Successive segments reuse the previously generated visual context while accepting updated controls (skeleton, camera trajectory, and text). Each block is produced by the few-step causal student, so the per-segment cost is bounded while retained context carries information across segments, enabling real-time long-horizon rollout.

Figure S7:Wide-FOV skeleton branch, example 1(four moments in time order; columns labeled above). Wide-FOV skeleton conditioning improves the alignment of the visible arm near the image boundary. Here the outer border-band keypoint error drops from 8.9 to 6.9 px, and the wide branch is closer to the ground truth on 91% of frames.

Figure S8:Wide-FOV skeleton branch, example 2(four moments in time order; columns labeled above). When the arm extends beyond the camera view, wide-FOV skeleton conditioning improves the prediction of its visible portion. Here the border-band keypoint error drops from 14.0 to 11.7 px, with the wide branch closer to the ground truth on 93% of frames.

Figure S9:Qualitative comparison on WorldArena(left: drawer + box; right: cup onto coaster). Each panel: five chronological frames (rows); columns areGT||Ropedia W0 (A14B)||BWM(TableS8). Ropedia W0 follows the commanded arm trajectory and completes the task like the ground truth (opening the drawer and placing the box, precisely seating the cup), whereas BWM’s arm drifts and under-moves (it never opens the drawer).
